ledger.claim: All three records are the same trip, so the rider's threshold showing is anchored: TRP-00514 appears on the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, and the trace window (10:36:40 to 10:58:40) sits inside the trip's recorded start and end. The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) - same trip identifier and matching pickup timing across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown - is satisfied before the excess is even reached.

Measured the way POL-RD-01 requires, the deviation is established and material. The governing figure is the trace length, trace_distance_km 11.75, not the trip record's rounded 11.8 km copy; against the booked optimal of 5.1 km the excess is 6.65 km, which is 130.4% of optimal. Both establishment tests pass (greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute), and the excess is additionally greater than 50% of optimal, so this is a MATERIAL deviation on the trace.

The trace the deviation rests on is clean for policy purposes and for schema purposes alike. EV-GPS-00514 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0, with 133 fixes at a 10 second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) fires - no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds - so the deviation may be established on the gps_trace alone, no corroboration under POL-RD-07(ii) is needed, and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is not engaged.

Nothing attributable to the rider produced this detour, so no exculpatory clause displaces the measured excess. The chat export for TRP-00514 holds zero messages, so POL-RD-04 has no rider instruction to run on and no waypoint_hint to corroborate; neither pickup_amended_at nor dropoff_amended_at is set and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-quote against; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. The excess survives every adjustment the policy offers the driver.

The driver's explanation - 'traffic on the direct road was heavy so I went around' - is discarded on this record. He names no traffic advisory, and the bundle contains none: EV-ADVIS-00514-01 is MISSING, carrying issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, admissibility weight 0.0 and no payload. Under POL-RD-13 the traffic assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else; with no advisory covering the trip window the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, that clause is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver cites no advisory evidence ID, the absent artifact is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not triggered. The deviation stands at the measured figure and POL-RD-02 runs against the booked optimal route.

The detour is not merely an inference from telemetry: the driver's own counterparty statement concedes the route - 'Traffic on the direct road was heavy so I went around.' The trip record and trace show what 'around' cost (11.75 km driven against a 5.1 km optimal), and the statement removes any dispute that the vehicle left the optimal corridor. What remains for the tribunal is only how much of the resulting fare the rider should bear.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretion. Under POL-RD-02 the recomputed fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 5.1 + 0.28 x 9.0) x the surge_multiplier of 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP or toll gantries on the optimal route, no fixed surcharge, waiting_time_fee 0.0 and promo_discount 0.0 - SGD 10.945. The charged total is SGD 19.61, so the refund is SGD 8.665, rounded UP to SGD 8.70 payable. At 44.19% of the charged total that is below the 90% full-refund share, and at SGD 8.70 it is far above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor, so the rider's remedy is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.70 and the remaining SGD 10.91 of the fare stands.

Because this is a MATERIAL deviation, the driver profile check under POL-RD-06 must be run, and the rider runs it openly: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so neither limb of the pattern test is met and no repeat-pattern uplift under POL-RD-06(b) is sought. The material finding rests on this trip's own trace under POL-RD-01, exactly as POL-GEN-01 requires, and the profile is used only for the test that names it.

The driver's explanation for the route is an external traffic cause, and the only clause that can test it is POL-RD-03, whose sole required artifact is a traffic_advisory. The bundle's traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00514-01, is MISSING — admissibility status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0 — so no advisory covers the optimal corridor for this trip window and the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run on the record. Because the driver invokes POL-RD-03 against that cited artifact and the artifact is missing from the pool, POL-RD-10(5) is engaged and the case must go to a human reviewer rather than produce a monetary ruling; the disputed $19.61 is then held rather than refunded. POL-RD-13(1) expressly preserves that consequence where the missing identifier is cited, and the driver cites it here.

This is not a repeat-deviation case and the FULL_REFUND uplift is not available. The material deviation requires the POL-RD-06 driver_profile check, but the pattern test fails on both its limbs: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, below the 3-flag limb, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 is a ratio of 0.00, far below the 0.05 limb with the required 40-trip base. With no pattern established, POL-RD-06(b) cannot raise the remedy above the ordinary POL-RD-02 partial, and POL-RD-06(c) cannot add a driver-conduct referral. Those two fields are the only profile fields the test permits.

If a monetary ruling does issue, it is capped by the POL-RD-02 arithmetic at $8.70 and cannot approach the $19.61 the rider contested. charged_total is $19.61. recomputed_fare is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 5.1 + 0.28 x 9.0) x 1.0 surge) + $0.80 platform fee = $10.9450. Refund = $19.61 - $10.9450 = $8.665, rounded up to $8.70, leaving $10.91 payable — 44.2% of the charged total, below the 90% share that would switch the outcome to a full refund. The rider's own benchmark of a 'nine dollar' ride is already met by the $10.91 payable, not exceeded by it.

The threshold is measured on the trace, and the trace gives the driver the lower, governing reading. gps_trace.trace_distance_km is 11.75 km, not the rounded 11.8 km convenience copy on the trip record, and POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the one that governs and forbids citing the rounded copy for the threshold test. On the trace figure the excess is 6.65 km, below the 8.0 km absolute materiality limb that would otherwise aggravate the finding.

No pass-through or statutory correction is added on top of the distance-and-time figure. The fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines (erp_gantries empty, tolls_erp 0.0), no airport surcharge (the trip did not ORIGINATE at an airport) and no waiting-time fee, so there is nothing to correct under POL-RD-09; and POL-RD-09(1) forbids adding any off-route ERP to the POL-RD-02 result, because such a charge is already comprehended in the recomputed fare and must never be counted twice.

The ledger reconciles line for line against the trip record and the trace — base fare 3.80 + distance 8.85 + time 6.16 + platform fee 0.80 = 19.61 over 11.8 charged kilometres — and no gantry or surcharge line lacks a counterpart in the trace or the trip record. There is therefore no billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09(4) and no referral on that ground.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the deviation is established on this trip's own clean trace, and the fare is recomputed accordingly. RIDER'S FIGURES AND THE DRIVER'S FALLBACK ARGUMENT AGREE, SO THE ARITHMETIC IS COMMON GROUND. The POL-RD-01 threshold is measured on the GPS trace. EV-GPS-00514 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0) records trace_distance_km 11.75, which POL-RD-01 makes govern over the trip record's rounded 11.8 km convenience copy. Against the booked optimal of 5.1 km (EV-TRIP-00514) the excess is 6.65 km, or 130.4% of optimal. Both establishment limbs pass (over 20% of optimal and over 0.8 km absolute), and because the excess also exceeds 50% of optimal this is a MATERIAL deviation, which required the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check. That check was run: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and 0 / 250 completed trips is 0.00, so neither limb of the repeat-pattern test is met; there is no POL-RD-06(b) FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) driver-conduct referral. The trace is not impaired: EV-GPS-00514 carries 133 fixes at a 10-second cadence, 100% coverage, no gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of POL-RD-07(a)-(c) fires and the deviation may stand on the trace alone. THE DRIVER'S TRAFFIC EXCUSE IS DISCARDED. Under POL-RD-13 a traffic assertion is tested against this trip's traffic_advisory and nothing else. The bundle's only advisory, EV-ADVIS-00514-01, is MISSING (issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0), so the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. I do NOT escalate this under POL-RD-10(5) as the driver asked: the asserting party named no advisory evidence ID, and POL-RD-13(1) provides that an assertion citing no artifact cannot be invoked against one - the absent advisory is a gap in the bundle, not a contradiction in it. Had the driver cited the missing identifier in his own account, escalation would have been required; he did not. NO EXCULPATORY ADJUSTMENT APPLIES. EV-CHAT-00514 holds zero messages, so POL-RD-04 has no rider instruction to run on; neither pickup_amended_at nor dropoff_amended_at is set and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 has no re-quote; vehicle_type is RYDE_X, so POL-RD-12's pooled baseline does not apply. REFUND ARITHMETIC UNDER POL-RD-02 (fare_model METERED; surge_multiplier 1.0 read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier): recomputed_fare = (3.80 + 0.75 x 5.1 + 0.28 x 9.0) x 1.0 + 0.80 platform fee = 10.945. charged_total = 19.61. Refund = 19.61 - 10.945 = 8.665, rounded UP to SGD 8.70. That is 44.19% of the charged total, below the 90% full-refund share, and above the SGD 0.50 de minimis, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 8.70; SGD 10.91 of the fare stands. No ERP, toll or surcharge lines exist to correct under POL-RD-09, and the ledger reconciles line for line against the trace and trip record (3.80 + 8.85 + 6.16 + 0.80 = 19.61) with no unmatched line, so there is no POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity referral. The rider's point that the trip was operated by a partner fleet is a customer-service matter and is not a ground under this policy; it does not change the fare computation.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
